items.note: Quasi-experiment in which college students solve a mathematical creativity task with ChatGPT or without it; mathematical creativity of solutions is scored, plus self-efficacy, interest, and metacognitive accuracy; N not in abstract; check overlap with the collected Liu (2025) study.

Pretest-posttest quasi-experiment with 215 preservice teachers (generative-AI vs traditional teaching-skills training); outcomes are teacher self-efficacy and higher-order thinking, with no creativity outcome on produced output (cited by a creativity meta-analysis, so a full-text check of the higher-order thinking scale may be warranted).

CHI 2026 system paper: controlled study (N=50) comparing stories co-written with the multi-persona NarrativeLoom system against a comparison condition; experts rated stories on Torrance fluency, flexibility, originality, elaboration; comparison condition and assignment (likely within-person) not stated; arXiv 2603.07155 is the same work.

480 Vietnamese undergraduates randomized to unaided control, unconstrained GenAI, or structured prompt-guided scaffolding on concept-generation and essay-design tasks; outputs scored by CAT expert panel, TTCT metrics, and semantic distance (originality d = -0.58 for unconstrained AI); conference proceedings, verify full text.

Between-subjects experiment with 221 employees manipulating proximal human-AI collaboration (high vs low); outcomes are idea selection and idea implementation behaviors, with idea originality as a moderator, so a creativity outcome on output is doubtful and the type of AI is not stated in the abstract.

Seven experiments (total n = 10,462; largest single experiment not stated) assigning people to learn a topic from LLM syntheses vs web search links, then write advice themselves; advice after LLM learning is sparser and less original (an after_ai-style comparison against another aid); abstract says experiments, random assignment per the search notes.

Longitudinal survey plus a randomized task-based experiment comparing supportive vs AI-substitutive generative-AI interaction on a creative thinking task; originality, semantic distance, fluency and flexibility measured; only the experiment is relevant and its N is not in the abstract.

Workshop quasi-experiment with 16 participants in four teams (12 ideas) comparing human-only ideation, unstructured AI, a structured prompting framework, and the framework with separated AI roles; ideas rated on fit, market potential, feasibility (quality, not novelty); far below 50 participants.

AEA RCT Registry entry only (AEARCTR-0016306, no linked paper or results): matchstick-form creative task with no assistance vs generative-AI assistance, judged on originality and elaboration; planned 50-70 adults and 50-70 children per arm; randomization by session schedule; next stage should look for a results paper.

Cohort quasi-experiment comparing a 2023 graduate cohort without and a 2024 cohort with JeepyTA (GPT-based teaching assistant) on ideation about educational uses of a video game; idea counts, quality, and uniqueness/homogeneity assessed; N not stated; OSF preprint DOI with journal version in Social Innovations Journal.
